title: How Bubbles tricked J. D. into learning his steps
summary: Green recalls trying to get Chuckles to learn Bubbles' style, Bubbles pretending to teach Green more, and his own spankings for inquisitiveness.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Don't -- in other -- other words, not to have too much hero worship. That's what he told me. See? But I was actually trying to help my partner, you understand, my childhood friend, which was -- I call him -- say he was south's favorite son, see as a child, understand? And he was known as Slim -- J. D., you know, he had a couple of names and the public called him this. And he had got a chance to expose being a professional because once -- once upon a time, there,

this -- the master of ceremonies of one of the shows -- he's about now, I think he's been helping me, what'd they call it, something about light -- the blind, you know, they called it something about the light -- the oh, it's some kind of organization of light, you know, about the blind, his name is Johnny Jazz Cousins. Well now his home state was Tennessee, rather his mother, you see, and he was master of ceremony -- a show at one of Tom Bailey's houses.

I think it was the A one. And that's where J.D. was popular, you see, in this city, Atlanta, Georgia. See? And -- he was -- he was building -- he was getting what we call first, you know, like an athlete continues to -- may have set a record, then he'll break the record, then he'll set another record, you know, like this. Now -- why he was a child, then, but I said somewhere earlier, in this -- recording that after Chuckles -- after -- after he got up here, after we got up into this part of the country, above the Mason-Dixon Line, see -- he was a -- he was giving himself other thoughts, other ideas, you know?

Why I was trying to learn or get Mr. Bubbles to teach me how to -- this tap dance, this new tap dance, he was creating, which was rhythm tap dancing, you see? He was -- I say he was fathering it, because he was so expert at it. You understand, he was -- it was like enlarging respiration, I would say that's the way he was to me -- other times, I mean

he would ask me questions, you know, and say things, what're you thinking about today? What's it all about, like that, you know? Being -- he's being a family head, he's like a family man, you see. And I would have to explain. You know, so I would say, Mr. Bubbles, you know I asked Mr. Buck about my -- my partner and how he could change his tap dancing, how he would be able to learn himself how to tap dance like you, at least a few of the steps, you know, because I mean the office is going to be insistent on us being little Buck and Bubbles, eventually, you know.

Say, he say, well, -- he decided right there that day, he said, well I tell you what, he said I'm going to pretend that I'll teach you more than I'm teaching him. Maybe that'll inspire -- that'll reawaken his anxieties, you know? See. I'm -- look here, I'm -- see -- I had a tendency to over -- you know, I would over like someone. I really would, you know, I didn't like to get caught at it, but I was. I had a great inquisitive nature or something, you see, I was always inquisitive, inquisitive, inquisitive -- asking questions, you know.

I used to get a lot of spankings from doing that, see? Until my father used to -- he put a stop to the spankings by having me to go to one of the brothers of the family, which was the Uncle (unintelligible) husband, you know, and I'd have to get a lecture, while I'm going -- you see?

Well now you see, eventually we worked it all out. See? And -- it worked out like Mr. Bubbles said. See? And Chuckles did learn a few of them, you know, but naturally he won't change his style, see? He didn't change his style because it's not easy, you know, it's a way of being versatile, you see and being able to be like what an impressionist is in voice, it can also happen in dance.
